Each stage has a clear gate. Do not skip ahead until the gate is passed for a factor/horizon.

column4: Gate to move to next stage

column3: Daily Snapshot Log grows by 1 real row every day (Turkey scrap, China HRC, BDI, iron ore, coking coal, LME CFR India, USD/INR, ingot/billet once tracked). No forward-fill, no approximation - only real observed values.
column4: GATE: at least 60 real daily observations per factor before testing it (roughly 3 months). Testing earlier = same leakage/overfitting risk we already found twice.

column3: For EACH factor separately: does it correlate with 8ANI's future move, at 15/30/60/90-day horizons? Use the factor's own trend/change as the input, 8ANI's forward change as the target.
column4: GATE: correlation must be statistically significant (p<0.05) AND survive PURGED validation (drop training rows whose target window overlaps the test window) - not just raw correlation, which we've shown can look real and vanish under purging.

column3: For factors that pass Stage 2: build a simple direction classifier (up/down) using ONLY that factor. Test at every horizon (5,10,15,20,30,45,60,90 days) to find exactly how many days in advance it has real predictive power, not just whether it does.
column4: GATE: report accuracy AND number of independent (non-overlapping) test points at the winning horizon. A factor 'passes' only if accuracy is real at a horizon with at least ~15-20 independent tests - fewer than that is not trustworthy, as we found with 60-90d single-combo results earlier.

column3: Only using factors that passed Stage 3: test combinations (pairs, triples) - NOT the full kitchen sink. Use the two-stage search framework already built (cheap Ridge ranking -> rigorous tree-model validation) so combinations are judged by DISTRIBUTION of results, not the single best (overfitting guard).
column4: GATE: VIF must be under 5 for all factors in the winning combination (checked explicitly - this is the exact mistake made early in this project, VIF up to 630). Reject any combination that fails this even if it scores well.

column3: Build the final model on the surviving factor combination. Bands come from the ACTUAL calibration-tested error distribution (checked to really cover 80%/50% as claimed - we already proved tight bands fail this test), not assumed.
column4: GATE: re-run calibration test before trusting any band. If band coverage is off, widen it - do not report a number known to be wrong.

column3: Every 2-4 weeks: re-run Stage 2-4 as new data arrives. Track whether the SAME factors keep winning (real signal) or the winners keep changing (overfitting/noise). Re-baseline if a policy shock or regime change occurs (e.g. new scrap policy, safeguard duty change).
column4: GATE: none - this stage runs forever, it is the maintenance loop.
